expand.arith-extensions.reason: Permissive throughout: "the shell may recognize arithmetic expressions beyond those listed", and it may use a wider signed integer type, or a real-floating type where that does not change the result. Nothing is required either way.

expand.assignment-redirection-environmen.reason: Explicitly unspecified: 'it is unspecified whether the expansions are carried out in the current execution environment or in the environment of the command about to be executed'.

expand.brace-implementation-defined.reason: Permissive: the word 'may be subject to an additional implementation-defined form of expansion'; no behaviour is required either way.

expand.cmdsub-redirections-only.reason: Explicitly unspecified: 'If the commands string consists solely of redirections, the results are unspecified'.

expand.cmdsub-terminating-paren.reason: Explicitly unspecified: "The behavior is unspecified if the terminating" right-parenthesis "is not present in the token containing the command substitution".

jobctl.background-job-brought-to-foregro.reason: Not an interactive-shell limitation -- the harness runs interactive cases on a pty with a controlling terminal, and the other job-control rules are now tested there. What is out of reach is TIMING against the tty: _run_pty writes the whole script in one payload, and the line discipline acts on a suspend character when the byte ARRIVES, not when the shell reads it, so a ^Z sent this way fires before the foreground job it was meant to stop exists. Suspensions driven by `kill -STOP` on a background job ARE tested (see cases_jobctl.py); this rule specifically requires a FOREGROUND job stopped from the terminal. Testable once _run_pty grows paced input.

jobctl.fg-terminal-settings-restore.reason: Not observable from the shell language: this is about state the shell holds across a suspend/resume -- saved termios, and the ordering of tcsetpgrp against SIGCONT inside fg -- for which the shell exposes no interface. The harness does have a controlling terminal (see cases_jobctl.py); that is not what is missing.

jobctl.foreground-job.reason: Requires observing that 'the whole list shall form a single foreground job up until the sequentially executed AND-OR lists have all completed', which is only visible through job-control bookkeeping in an interactive session.

jobctl.non-interactive-message-timing.reason: Permissive: 'the same message may also be written by a non-interactive shell, at any of the following times'; nothing is required either way.

param.nlspath.reason: [XSI] 'Determine the location of message catalogs for the processing of LC_MESSAGES'; observable only on an XSI system with a message catalog installed.

param.positional-zero-not-positional.reason: Explicitly unspecified: "the results of expanding `${00}` are unspecified". The classification of 0 as a special parameter rather than a positional one is asserted by param.special-parameters and param.special-zero.

param.pwd-assignment.reason: Permissive and unspecified: 'Assignments to the PWD variable may be ignored. If an application sets or unsets the value of PWD, the behaviors of the cd and pwd utilities are unspecified'.

pattern.invalid-byte-sequence-unspecifie.reason: Explicitly unspecified: matching a string containing bytes that "do not form part of a valid character, the behavior is unspecified".

pattern.leading-period-in-bracket-unspec.reason: Explicitly unspecified: "It is unspecified whether an explicit <period> in a bracket expression matching list" can match a leading period in a filename.

pattern.trailing-backslash-unspecified.reason: Explicitly unspecified: 'If a pattern ends with an unescaped <backslash>, the behavior is unspecified'.

pattern.unmatched-open-bracket-unspecifi.reason: Explicitly unspecified: "it is unspecified whether other unquoted" pattern characters "within the same slash-delimited component of the pattern retain their special meanings or are treated as ordinary characters".

quote.dollar-single-quotes-null-byte.reason: Explicitly unspecified: "it is unspecified whether that null byte is included in the result" or whether it and everything after it up to the closing quote is evaluated and discarded.

quote.dollar-single-quotes-octal-overflo.reason: Explicitly unspecified: an octal escape that "will not fit in a byte, the results are unspecified".

quote.dollar-single-quotes-undefined-esc.reason: Explicitly unspecified: 'The behavior of an unescaped <backslash> immediately followed by any other character, including <newline>, is unspecified'.

quote.dollar-single-quotes-unencodable.reason: For a character with no encoding in the current locale "the result is implementation-defined"; the one normative constraint (implementations shall not substitute bytes that do not form valid characters) is vacuous in the C locale the harness fixes, where every byte is a valid character.

quote.double-quotes-backquote-undefined.reason: Explicitly undefined: 'Either of the following cases produces undefined results'.

quote.future-special-characters.reason: Advisory about a possible future revision, addressed to applications: "A future version of this standard may extend the conditions under which the conditionally-special characters are special." Nothing is required of the shell.

redir.here-doc-fd-type.reason: Explicitly unspecified: 'It is unspecified whether the file descriptor a here-document is supplied on is opened as a regular file or some other type of file'.

redir.location-format.reason: Permissive and implementation-defined: "The shell may support an additional format used for redirection", and if it is supported its behavior is implementation-defined.

redir.output-noclobber-atomicity.reason: Atomicity is not falsifiable from the shell language, and the two shell-visible clauses are both permissive: the open operation "need not fail with [EEXIST]" when the target is a symbolic link that does not resolve to an existing regular file, and "The check for the type of the file need not be performed atomically" with the rest.

shell.hashbang-unspecified.reason: Explicitly unspecified: if the first line of a file of shell commands starts with a <number-sign> followed by an <exclamation-mark>, "the results are unspecified".

signal.pending-trap-order.reason: Explicitly unspecified: 'the order of execution of trap actions is unspecified'.

token.alias-reserved-word-unspecified.reason: Explicitly unspecified: 'it is unspecified whether the TOKEN is subject to alias substitution'.

token.reserved-words-optional.reason: Permissive and unspecified: the listed words '[[', ']]', 'function', 'namespace', 'select', 'time' 'may be recognized as reserved words, in which case the results are unspecified'.

token.reserved-words-trailing-colon.reason: Explicitly unspecified: words ending in <colon> are reserved and 'their use in those circumstances produces unspecified results'.
